# Summary of Cairn Rules

## Pulses
A pulse makes a cairn grow. The growth amount is the stride plus a bonus based on how tall the cairn already is. Specifically, you count how many complete stride-sized chunks fit into the current height, and add that count as bonus growth. Taller cairns grow more from a pulse than shorter ones.

When applying multiple pulses in sequence, each one recalculates the stride count based on the new height after the previous pulse. You can't reuse the same stride count for every pulse—this is a common mistake.

## Leaks
A leak causes a cairn to lose marks after pulsing. You first apply the pulse normally, then the leak takes effect on the resulting height. The leak size determines how many marks are lost: for every complete leak-sized chunk in the pulsed height, one mark is removed.

## Drains
A drain is like a leak but happens in cycles. Each cycle consists of a pulse followed by a fixed amount of marks being removed. The cairn grows from the pulse but loses the drain amount afterward. Over time, if the drain is large enough, the cairn will eventually shrink to zero, though this typically takes many cycles because pulses tend to add substantial growth.

## Origins (Working Backwards)
You can reverse the pulse process to find what height a cairn started at before experiencing pulses. You work backwards cycle by cycle, solving the equation: old height plus its full strides count equals the result you're working from.

## Merging Cairns
Two cairns combine using weighted shares and a tether value. Each cairn contributes based on its share (proportions that sum to 1). You take the floor of each weighted contribution and add them together. Then you apply a bonus based on the shorter cairn (one mark per ten marks). Finally, the tether is added—this can be positive or negative.
